messages:
jordan: FYI noticed a p99 tail regression after yesterday's kernel-fallback tweak. r4g-small pool, steady qps, but tails jumped when KV miss hit + microbatches were small.
maria: can you share a short perf sample or trace?
jordan: pasted capture below, short summary: p50 ~ 45ms, p95 ~ 110ms (ok), p99 480ms -> 780ms after change. looks correlated with fallback to slower kernel on cold kv cache.

jordan: trace snippet (reduced):
```
kernel_select: fast_mm -> fallback_scalar (12% requests)
kv_cache: miss (prefix miss) -> warmup latency + respawn
microbatch: size=1..3, queue_wait=6ms
latency_breakdown: enqueue 4ms | kernel_setup 18ms | kv_miss_wait 120ms | exec 30ms | tail_retries 600ms
```

alex: interesting — looks like two things: (1) fallback causes a big exec/handshake step, (2) small microbatches mean more exposure to kv_miss variance. Try to reduce kernel flip frequency with hysteresis and raise max_batch_tokens to let more requests join the fast path.

maria: can we tune scheduler params quickly? what if we try:
```
scheduler:
  max_batch_tokens: 3072
  max_wait_ms: 6
  hysteresis_ms: 4
```

kevin: ran a short experiment on a canary node: increased max_batch_tokens -> p99 dropped ~120ms, p95 unchanged. But throughput transiently decreased when bursty small requests arrived (some extra packing overhead).

jordan: thanks. also observed kv hit-rate drop during bursts, maybe due to cache eviction/ttl. adding hysteresis helped reduce kernel swap chatter per alex.

maria: question — do we have a cheap flag to avoid fallback for microbatch<=2? We could prefer slower kernel only when batch size >= threshold to avoid switching for tiny requests.

alex: yeah we can gate fallback by effective_batch_tokens: if batch_tokens < 512 then prefer fast_mm even if marginally suboptimal to avoid handshake cost. simple policy change.

kevin: I pushed a small config patch to canary: `fallback_min_batch_tokens: 512` + `hysteresis_ms: 4`. deploy-bot shows successful rollout for 3 nodes.
deploy-bot: rollout: canary group updated (3 nodes). no errors.

jordan: after canary run (30m): p99 down from 780ms -> 360ms. microburst tail smoothed. KV miss penalty still present but less amplified by kernel flip.
maria: nice. next steps: (1) run 24h canary, (2) collect kv hit histograms, (3) run full cluster A/B for a business hour to validate throughput economics.
alex: also add a small metric: kernel_swap_rate per minute + kv_miss_latency histogram so we can alert when swap_rate spikes.

kevin: note for release notes: we changed scheduler heuristics (fallback gating + hysteresis) and bumped default max_batch_tokens. preflight perf tests show tail improvement at mild cost to peak throughput in some synthetic burst patterns.
jordan: agree. I created a quickboard with p50/p95/p99, kernel_swap_rate, kv_hit_rate to watch. link: https://internal.redwood/boards/rt/scheduler-hysteresis
maria: awesome, will follow up with a runbook entry for oncall (how to revert params and what thresholds to watch). :thumbsup:
